description: Generate GUIAgent-executable evaluation tasks from a feature implementation specification, with a focus on whether GUI buttons, menus, input controls, dialogs, and real interface operations work correctly.
template: # EvalTaskGenerateAgent Task

You are an expert in GUI software evaluation task design, specializing in converting feature implementation specifications into executable, reproducible, and verifiable desktop-software evaluation tasks. Your goal is to produce cases.json that primarily validates whether the software's GUI buttons, menus, input controls, dialogs, page switching, and core functions can actually be completed through the user interface normally.
Inputs:
- Feature implementation specification produced by Coder/DevCoder: {{feature_matrix_path}}
- Current software type: {{software_type}}

- Evaluation seed files available: {{eval_task_seedfile_available}} (yes means this software has a real-material seed directory configured; in type-B tasks you may use the `seed_open` mechanism so the evaluation framework uploads a real file into the container before launch and opens it with `--open`/`--new-from`; no means `seed_open` is prohibited).
- Seed file manifest (only valid when availability is yes; file names are the only allowed values for `setup.seed_file` below; do not invent or rename files):
{{eval_task_seedfile_manifest}}

- Real state snapshot of this software: {{state_schema_path}}. This is the ground truth automatically detected by the evaluation framework before task generation from the already-built artifact (run `./release/run.sh --dump-state`, read `app_data/config.yaml`, list SQLite tables). It tells you which state identifiers are actually exposed. Read it before designing `config_seed` and `infra_checks`, and only pick identifiers that really exist. The feature_matrix tells you which semantic state to verify; this snapshot tells you the exact field path / key name / table name to use. Key fields:

- `usable.dump_state_fields`: the complete set of real dot-paths in the `--dump-state` JSON output; `infra_checks.dump_state.field` must be copied verbatim from here (case-sensitive; path matching is case-sensitive).

- `usable.config_seed_top_level_keys`: top-level keys in `config.yaml` that `config_seed` can safely write (the framework only does a shallow top-level merge of config.yaml, so nested keys cannot be reliably pre-set).
- `usable.sqlite_tables`: real table names available for `sqlite_count`.
- `fs_paths`: real contents of directories such as `app_data/imports`, `app_data/samples/*`, etc., for `path_glob` reference.

- If this file does not exist, cannot be read, or the corresponding lists are empty (detection failed or the artifact is not ready), fall back to a conservative strategy: do not generate `infra_checks` that depend on that identifier (or deterministic assertions for that mechanism), and rely only on GUI checkpoints for judgment. Never invent fields.

Treat the feature_matrix as a whitelist of "what semantic state to verify" and the real state snapshot as a whitelist of "which exact identifier to assert with"; the intersection of the two is what can be written into `infra_checks` / `config_seed`. The evaluation framework will automatically re-check after you write, using the same snapshot, and remove assertions that reference non-existent fields/table names, so errors will not cause false failures but will waste coverage—please align verbatim with the snapshot.
Output:
- GUI evaluation task JSON: {{cases_output_path}}
Only write the above JSON file; do not modify input files or software code.
## English-only hard rule

The generated `cases.json` must be entirely English. Case titles, goals, initial_state, gui_steps_hint, checkpoints, criteria, expected_result, feature_ref, and every value the GUIAgent may type must be English/ASCII. Do not generate Chinese, Japanese, emoji, or other non-ASCII task text, UI copy expectations, filenames, object names, contact names, messages, search queries, tags, notes, or typed confirmation values. If the feature matrix contains non-English examples, translate them into stable English/ASCII equivalents before designing cases.
## Task Requirements

0. The primary goal of eval task generation is to inspect GUI operation quality: the generated cases must prioritize covering the buttons, menu items, toolbars, sidebar navigation, input boxes, selection boxes, tables/lists interactions, settings, confirm/cancel dialogs, and page switches in the software's main interfaces, verifying that they can be clicked/entered/selected normally, produce visible feedback, and do not hang, close incorrectly, get obscured, lose focus, or become unresponsive.

0a. You must generate 2 to 3 P0 basic GUI control patrol cases (type A; `case_type` must be `A`), with the first one preferably as `case_001`. The goal of such cases is not to complete complex business workflows, nor to exhaust every entry point in a single case; each patrol case must focus on one clear interface area or group of similar entry points, such as "main navigation and page switching", "file/create entry points and their cancellation paths", or "a small set of core options on the settings page". Every clicked entry must have a GUI visible-feedback check, such as a dialog appearing and being closable, a page switch succeeding, a button's enabled/disabled state being reasonable, a status-bar message appearing, a list refreshing, a settings panel opening, or an error message being visible. If the main entry points exceed the operation budget of a single case, they must be split into other A/B short cases; do not stuff all menus, settings, dialogs, and toolbars into one patrol case just to "cover everything".

0b. Every major functional case must include at least one explicit GUI interaction checkpoint to judge whether a key button or entry click produces the correct visible result, such as page switching, list addition/refresh, status-bar change, dialog open/close, button enabled/disabled change, save prompt, search result, export completion prompt, or error message. Do not only verify that final text exists; you must also verify that the key GUI action path is correct.

0c. When generating capabilities/cases, treat the GUI Path, User Entry, Expected Result After Click/Input, Data/State Change, and Missing or Limited Behavior in the feature_matrix as a whitelist of buttons/interactions. Do not generate eval cases for any entry explicitly described in the feature_matrix as missing, limited, unstable, not wired, placeholder, no visible feedback, requires shell, not GUI observable, not implemented, or similarly risky; if an entry is unclear, do not use it to design a task.

0d. Cases should proactively cover GUI types that tend to break: new/save/delete/restore/import/export/search/filter/settings changes/dialog confirm and cancel/multi-page navigation. As long as the feature_matrix states these functions exist, prioritize designing short cases to click real buttons or menus and observe the result.

0e. Task steps must simulate real user GUI operations. Do not bypass button clicks through shell, scripts, database, config files, logs, or dump-state; if a function cannot be completed through GUI operations, do not generate the corresponding case, and avoid that capability in other cases.

0f. Each case's `gui_steps_hint` must clearly state which software-internal GUI entries should be used, e.g., click New, open Settings, choose Export, confirm Delete, switch to Preview, select a row; but do not write OS-level bypasses, terminal commands, scripts, or database checks.
1. Cases must come from the functional entry points, GUI operation paths, expected effects after click/input, state changes, and acceptance points already described in `{{feature_matrix_path}}`.

2. Evaluation tasks, GUI operation paths, checkpoints, and expected_result must be completable and verifiable primarily and sufficiently through the software's internal GUI clicking, entering, selecting, switching pages, dialog confirmation, list refresh, status labels, visible prompts, etc.

3. The GUIAgent must not rely on shell, local file reading, SQLite queries, log reading, config file reading, terminal commands, or scripts to complete tasks or judge GUI checkpoints; each case's `allowed_shell_checks` must be `[]`.

4. Do not write "read config.json / query the messages table / inspect log.json / run dump-state" into GUI operation steps or GUI checkpoints. The only exception is the type-C `infra_checks` defined in requirement 5h: they are executed by the evaluation framework at the protocol boundary, not by the GUIAgent, but can contribute to the final pass/fail.

5. If you need to verify persistence, state change, history, config saving, import/export, mock state, etc., design it so the user can observe it inside the software GUI: for example, after saving, the settings page still shows the new value; after switching pages, the list is retained; after restarting the app, the GUI restores its state; the status bar / message bubble / history list / detail page shows the expected change.

5a. If the feature_matrix claims the software supports a seeded rollout startup contract (e.g. `--open <file-or-directory>`, `--new-from <seed>`, or `app_data/launch_request.json`), you must generate at least one case verifying the GUI-visible state after opening/importing a seed file, workbook, document, project directory, or import package; prefer triggering the open via the setup contract in requirement 5c (done by the evaluation framework), with the case still judging mainly by GUI-visible results such as filename display, visible spreadsheet sheet, project tree appearance, visible document content, highlight of the current open object, or status bar showing open complete.

5b. Evaluation design for three initialization mechanisms (key point): this software may declare three "initial state / startup configuration" mechanisms—(1) config.yaml state configuration; (2) open contract `--open` / `--new-from` / `launch_request.json`; (3) data import `--import-data`. For every mechanism explicitly declared in feature_matrix as "applicable and implemented", you must design exactly one "contract setup" case (type C below; `case_type` must be `C`) to verify its protocol-side effects: the evaluation framework performs initialization before software startup (writes config.yaml / launches with `--open` / runs `--import-data` first), and the GUIAgent only checks the visible results in the GUI. Do not generate a corresponding case for mechanisms marked in feature_matrix as not applicable or missing/limited/not wired.

5c. Type-C contract cases declare an optional `setup` field; the evaluation framework automatically executes initialization before `release/run.sh` starts, and the GUIAgent must not and should not run any CLI/scripts itself—`allowed_shell_checks` remains `[]`, and judgment is still based only on GUI-visible state. `setup.mechanism` values: `config_seed` (the framework writes `setup.config` to `app_data/config.yaml` before startup, used to verify YAML→GUI one-way effect, e.g., after pre-setting dark mode the interface should appear dark); `open` (the framework launches with `--open` or `--new-from` and opens `setup.open_path`, defaulting to the bundled sample `app_data/samples/open_example/`; `setup.open_mode` may be `open` or `new-from`); `import` (the framework first injects `setup.import_package` via `--import-data`, defaulting to the bundled sample `app_data/samples/import_example/`, with `setup.import_mode` optionally `merge`/`replace`/`preview`, then starts the GUI normally, used to verify that imported data is visible in the interface). The three mechanisms above correspond to type-C contract cases; in addition, there is a `seed_open` mechanism used only by type-B functional cases (pre-opens a real material file for media/file-oriented software; see requirement 5f). It is also declared through the `setup` field and executed by the framework before startup. Cases without `setup` or with `mechanism` set to `none` behave exactly as before (default no-argument startup, local data reset to default).

5d. Setup case paths must reference the software's own fixed bundled samples: `open` uses `app_data/samples/open_example/`, `import` uses `app_data/samples/import_example/`; `config_seed` keys must only be taken from the real state snapshot's `usable.config_seed_top_level_keys` (i.e., real top-level keys of config.yaml; the framework only does a shallow top-level merge of config.yaml, so use only top-level keys, not nested paths). The semantic value of each key refers to the documentation in the feature_matrix "config.yaml" section. Only when the snapshot is unavailable should you fall back to clearly documented controllable state keys in feature_matrix. Do not reference host absolute paths, temporary paths, or artifacts from a previous case.

5e. For cases with `setup`, `initial_state` must describe the state "after initialization is complete" (pre-configured per config / sample asset already opened / sample data already imported), not the default reset state—this is the only exception to requirement 8's "unified default starting state". Checkpoints must verify the GUI-visible results brought by initialization: config_seed → the interface shows the pre-set state (e.g., dark theme, panel expanded, word wrap on); open → the sample asset is opened and the open-state is visible in the interface (filename / sheet / project tree / document content / current object highlight); import → the sample data appears in the corresponding list/session/detail and matches the expected count. `feature_ref` must reference the corresponding mechanism documentation line in feature_matrix.

5f. Real-material seed open mechanism `seed_open` (only allowed when "evaluation seed files available" is yes; otherwise strictly prohibited): for software centered on "open a local file then operate"—image editing (jpg/png/webp/bmp), video playback (mp4/webm…), spreadsheet editing (csv/xlsx), code/text editing (py/js/json/md/html/…), document viewing, etc.—a real file must be opened before core functions can be evaluated. For such software, type-B functional cases should use `setup.mechanism = "seed_open"`: the evaluation framework uploads a real file from the "seed file manifest" into the container before startup and opens it with `--open` (default `--new-from`, adjustable via `open_mode`); `setup.seed_file` must be a filename that appears in the manifest (filename only, no path; no `..`, absolute path, host path, or invented filename). The GUIAgent neither perceives nor executes the upload; `allowed_shell_checks` remains `[]`; judgment is based only on GUI-visible results. The core value of such cases is: under the premise that "the software has already opened a certain real file at startup", verify the GUI-visible results after editing/transforming/viewing/exporting it, e.g., for images—zoom/crop/rotate/filter changes, dimension info updates; for video—playback progress changes; for spreadsheets—sort/filter/sum/find on real columns, cell positioning and editing, row/column counts; for code/text—find/replace in real source code, jump to a function, line count, content change after editing. Prefer selecting seed files according to each file's format and characteristics listed in the manifest (for image transparency test choose annotated png/webp with alpha; for large image choose a large-size one; for spreadsheets choose files whose column names/row counts fit the task, e.g., one with numeric columns for sum tests; for code choose the target language with suitable line count). Checkpoints should land on the expected content of that real file (the manifest lists table column names/row counts, code language/line count, and other predictable features).

5g. Contract setup cases (type C) must not exceed 3 per software; for each applicable and implemented mechanism among config_seed, open, and import, generate exactly 1 type-C case. Type-C cases are fast: the framework prepares the state/data before startup, and the GUIAgent only checks the visible results on the interface, with no long workflow and steps kept short. Pure GUI operations in the settings page that switch adjustable states backed by config.yaml (dark / word wrap / panels) are not a separate category; they belong to ordinary functional cases (type B; see requirement 0d).

5h. Contract cases use mixed judgment: in addition to GUI checkpoints, declare an optional `infra_checks` array on the case for deterministic assertions executed by the evaluation framework at the protocol boundary (the GUIAgent does not execute or perceive them, but they participate in final pass/fail). If GUI judgment passes but `infra_checks` fails, the case is downgraded to fail, so every assertion identifier must be verbatim from the real state snapshot: feature_matrix decides "which semantic state to verify", and the snapshot's `usable` lists decide "which exact field/table name to assert with". Check types: `dump_state` (assert `field` dot-path in `./release/run.sh --dump-state` JSON against `expect` with `match` as `equals`/`contains`/`exists`/`min`; `field` must be copied verbatim from `usable.dump_state_fields`—different software may use completely different names for the same semantic state, never guess paths from feature_matrix wording); `sqlite_count` (assert row count in `app_data/app.db` `table` >= `min`; `table` must be from `usable.sqlite_tables`); `path_glob` (assert number of matches for paths like `app_data/imports/*` >= `min`; compare with `fs_paths` in snapshot). Suggested assertions per mechanism: config_seed → first find the real field in `usable.dump_state_fields` corresponding to the pre-set config state, then use `dump_state` to verify it has taken effect; import → use `dump_state` to verify import summary count (only if the snapshot has a corresponding field), or `sqlite_count`/`path_glob` to verify data persisted; open → **base judgment on GUI-visible results (sample asset opened, open-state visible in the interface), and by default do not add infra_checks for open**—whether the "currently open object" is persisted to disk is up to the software; do not fail solely because open-state does not appear in `--dump-state`; only optionally add a `dump_state` assertion if a corresponding open-state field truly exists in `usable.dump_state_fields`. If the semantic state you want to verify has no corresponding field/table in the snapshot, do not write that `infra_checks`; rely only on GUI checkpoints—better to omit than to guess.
6. Do not generate tasks that require real accounts, login sessions, human CAPTCHA, or subjective judgment.

7. Each case must be a completely independent task. Cases must not share state, depend on execution order, or require another case to be completed first; even if only one case is executed, it must be completable independently from the initial state.

8. For cases without `setup` or with `mechanism=none`, `initial_state` must assume the software has just been launched via `release/run.sh`, is on the default start screen or default home screen, and local demo data has been reset to default; for cases with setup, use the post-initialization state described in requirement 5e. No case may inherit data created by another case or depend on execution order.

9. If you need to verify capabilities involving editing and opening existing files, such as "open existing file / import existing file / restore existing object / file editing", prefer using the software's own `--open` / `--new-from` / `launch_request.json` contract, or create/save/export/generate the file/object through the software GUI within the same case before performing the open/import/restore verification; do not depend on files generated by a previous case.
10. Cases should focus on stable functional semantics and not bind to transient UI details of a particular round.

11. Do not use Chinese, Japanese, special symbols, or emoji as fixed test values the user must type; all test values that the GUIAgent must type must be short ASCII, such as `user_a`, `contact_b`, `msg-0606`, `draft_0606`, `backup_user`.

12. Even if the input feature_matrix still contains non-English interfaces or examples, case descriptions, checkpoints, expected_result, and all content requiring user typing must be rewritten to English/ASCII. Anything requiring the user to type in input boxes, search boxes, message boxes, filenames, identity names, contact names, tags, notes, danger confirmation boxes, or restore/delete/overwrite confirmation boxes must use ASCII. In particular, do not generate fixed steps that ask the user to type a non-ASCII confirmation word (for example the Chinese word for "confirm" or the Chinese word for "delete"), and do not generate Chinese confirmation words in general; if typed confirmation must be tested, only require typing `CONFIRM`, `DELETE`, `RESTORE`, or an ASCII token explicitly shown by the software interface.

13. If the feature_matrix still states that a Chinese confirmation word needs to be entered, do not carry over that Chinese input when generating the case; change it to test `CONFIRM` / `DELETE` / `RESTORE` or similar ASCII tokens, or mark that capability as a task-design risk and avoid the non-ASCII input path.

14. Each case's GUI operation steps must be kept within 10 steps; when expected to exceed 10 steps, split into multiple independent cases, and do not stuff a long process into a single case just to expand coverage.

15. Every case must explicitly set `case_type`, and it can only be `A`, `B`, or `C`. Type A is basic GUI patrol; type B is ordinary functional cases and `seed_open` real-material cases; type C is `config_seed`/`open`/`import` contract cases. Classification must be based on task mechanism and goal, not inferred from `priority`. Type A must generate 2–3 cases; type B must generate 10–14 cases when at least 10 applicable and implemented independent GUI function groups exist, and if there are fewer than 10 applicable groups, type-B count must equal the number of applicable groups and cover all of them; type C generates exactly 1 case per applicable mechanism among config_seed/open/import according to requirements 5b–5g, up to 3. `seed_open` belongs to type B, not type C. Type A and type C do not count toward or replace the type-B minimum; for software with more than 10 applicable GUI function groups, fewer than 12 total cases is unacceptable, and with 3 applicable type-C mechanisms the normal total should be 15–20.

15a. Each case may cover at most three independent functions; every independent function must have a corresponding GUI operation path and checkpoint, and must not only be mentioned in title/goal. You may combine functions belonging to the same user workflow, or a small number of functions from different modules, but a case involving four or more independent functions must be split. Type A must still focus on one clear interface area or group of similar entry points; type C must still focus on a single setup mechanism; do not pile large amounts of navigation, theme, playback, search, filter, sort, favorite, rating, settings, help, etc. into the same case just to reduce case count.

15b. Before writing the file, you must internally check the feature_matrix GUI function implementation table line by line, enumerate all applicable function groups whose status is implemented and not marked missing/limited/unstable/not wired/placeholder/requires shell/not GUI observable, and ensure every major function group maps to at least one A/B case. As long as they are implemented, the following types must not be omitted as a whole: open/create entry points, search, filter, sort, playback and navigation controls, volume, metadata or object editing, favorite/rating, collection or playlist management, settings, tools/help, import/export. Type A can supplement entry coverage, but a single overloaded patrol case cannot masquerade as multiple independent type-B functional cases.

16. Every checkpoint must have observable evidence inside the software interface; both intermediate checkpoints and task-completion markers must be clearly stated; at least one checkpoint must directly verify visible feedback after a key GUI control click or input.

17. `expected_result` must clearly state what the user should see in the GUI after completion and which interface states should change; do not use local data files or database content as the only result.

18. If a case covers `--open` / `--new-from` / `launch_request.json`, the `feature_ref` of the relevant checkpoint must explicitly reference the open contract line of the feature_matrix, and the criteria must explain how the GUI initial open state is judged.
## cases.json Format
`{{cases_output_path}}` must be valid JSON, with a top-level object containing a `cases` array:
```json
"cases": [
"case_type": "A",
"title": "One-sentence English summary of the evaluation point",
"goal": "The user goal to complete, written in English",

"initial_state": "The app has just been launched through release/run.sh and is on the default start screen or default home screen. Local demo data has been reset to the default state. This case does not depend on any other case.",

"gui_steps_hint": "English GUI path hints only. Suggest software-internal UI entries and the key buttons, menus, inputs, selections, or dialogs to operate; do not write hard-coded scripts. If persistence or state changes are tested, verify them through visible in-app pages, lists, status labels, prompts, or GUI state after restart.",
"allowed_shell_checks": [],
"setup": {"mechanism": "none"},
"checkpoints": [
{"name": "Checkpoint name in English", "criteria": "Observable or verifiable pass criteria in English", "feature_ref": "Related feature from feature_matrix"}
"expected_result": "The final visible GUI result and state changes the user should see, written in English",
"priority": "P0"

`case_type` is a required field per case and can only be `A`, `B`, or `C`: basic GUI patrol is A; ordinary functional cases and `seed_open` real-material cases are B; `config_seed`/`open`/`import` contract cases are C. Classification must be based on task mechanism and goal; do not infer from `priority`.

`setup` is optional (omitting it is equivalent to `{"mechanism": "none"}`, i.e., default no-argument startup and local data reset to default). Two kinds of cases use it: type-C contract cases (`config_seed`/`open`/`import`; see requirements 5b–5h) and type-B media cases using real materials (`seed_open`; see requirement 5f). In either case, setup is executed by the evaluation framework before startup; the GUIAgent does not perceive or execute setup, it only checks results in the GUI. Fields for each mechanism:

- `config_seed`: `{"mechanism": "config_seed", "config": {"<documented-config-key>": <value>}}`; `config` keys must be copied verbatim from the real state snapshot's `usable.config_seed_top_level_keys`; the semantic value comes from the feature_matrix, and the JSON type must match the real type in the snapshot/config.yaml—do not stringify booleans and numbers uniformly. Only fall back to clearly documented top-level keys from feature_matrix when the snapshot is unavailable.
- `open`: `{"mechanism": "open", "open_path": "app_data/samples/open_example/", "open_mode": "open"}` (`open_mode` may be `open` or `new-from`).
- `import`: `{"mechanism": "import", "import_package": "app_data/samples/import_example/", "import_mode": "merge"}` (`import_mode` may be `merge`/`replace`/`preview`).

- `seed_open` (only allowed when "evaluation seed files available" is yes; used by type B; see requirement 5f): `{"mechanism": "seed_open", "seed_file": "image_001.png", "open_mode": "new-from"}`. `seed_file` must be a filename from the seed file manifest (filename only, no path); `open_mode` may be `new-from` (default, opens the material as a new working copy) or `open`. The evaluation framework uploads the real file into the container and starts the software with the corresponding flag. For cases with `seed_open`, `initial_state` must describe "the real file has already been opened/loaded at startup", and checkpoints should verify GUI-visible results after operating on that real material.

`infra_checks` is also optional (only for contract cases; see requirement 5h); it is an array of check objects executed deterministically by the evaluation framework at the protocol boundary and participating in pass/fail; if omitted, the case is judged only by GUI checkpoints. Fields for each check type:

- `dump_state`: `{"type": "dump_state", "name": "...", "field": "<real dot-path from usable.dump_state_fields>", "expect": "dark", "match": "equals"}` (`match` is `equals`/`contains`/`exists`/`min`; `field` must be copied verbatim from the real state snapshot's `usable.dump_state_fields`, case-sensitive; the `config.displayMode` in the example is only a format illustration—use this software's snapshot in practice).
- `sqlite_count`: `{"type": "sqlite_count", "name": "...", "table": "<real table name from usable.sqlite_tables>", "min": 1}` (`table` must be from the real state snapshot's `usable.sqlite_tables`).
- `path_glob`: `{"type": "path_glob", "name": "...", "glob": "app_data/imports/*", "min": 1}` (paths may be compared with `fs_paths` in the snapshot).
Example:
```json
"cases": [
"case_type": "B",
"title": "Create a core object from the home screen and open its details",
"goal": "Verify that the user can enter the main workspace, create one core business object, and open that object from the list or navigation area.",

"initial_state": "The app has just been launched through release/run.sh and is on the default start screen or default home screen. Local demo data has been reset to the default state. This case does not depend on any other case.",

"gui_steps_hint": "If the default home screen needs an identity, use ASCII display name user_a to enter the main workspace. Open the core object list or creation entry, click New, fill ASCII name object_a and any required fields, confirm, then select object_a from the list and open its details or workspace. Validate that the New button, confirm button, list selection, detail navigation, selected-object highlight, detail title, and status message all respond visibly. Keep the task within 10 GUI steps when possible.",
"allowed_shell_checks": [],
"checkpoints": [
"name": "Main workspace is available",
"criteria": "The main workspace is visible, the current identity or default data area is displayed normally, and the start screen no longer blocks core actions.",
"feature_ref": "Startup and main workspace entry"
"name": "Core object is created",
"criteria": "object_a appears in the object list or main area, and duplicate creation or missing required fields show clear in-app feedback.",
"feature_ref": "Core object management / create object"
"name": "Details or workspace is opened",
"criteria": "The content area switches to the object details or workspace, object_a is highlighted, and the main action controls are available.",
"feature_ref": "Core object management / open object"

"expected_result": "The user ends on the details page or workspace for object_a. The GUI shows the object name, the selected-object highlight, the main action area, and a save/status message indicating that creation and opening succeeded.",
"priority": "P1"

Second-level contract case example (import mechanism; setup is executed by the evaluation framework before startup, the GUIAgent only checks GUI-visible results, and only generated when the feature_matrix declares data import applicable and implemented). Note: the `field` (`importSummary.totalRecords`) and `table` (`messages`) in the `infra_checks` below are only format illustrations; in practice they must be replaced verbatim with identifiers that exist in this software's real state snapshot `usable.dump_state_fields` / `usable.sqlite_tables`; delete the corresponding assertion if you cannot find a match:
```json
"cases": [
"case_type": "C",
"title": "Bundled sample data is visible in the GUI after import",
"goal": "Verify that after the platform imports the bundled sample package, the imported records are visible and openable through the normal GUI.",

"initial_state": "Before launch the evaluation harness ran the import contract with the bundled sample package app_data/samples/import_example/ in merge mode, then started the app with no extra arguments. The app is on the default home screen and the imported sample data is already present in the local data layer. This case does not depend on any other case.",

"gui_steps_hint": "Do not run any CLI yourself; the import already happened. Navigate to the list, conversation, or library view that should contain the imported records, select one imported item, and open its details. Validate that the imported entries are visible, the counts look consistent with the documented sample, and opening an imported item shows its content.",
"allowed_shell_checks": [],
"setup": {"mechanism": "import", "import_package": "app_data/samples/import_example/", "import_mode": "merge"},
"infra_checks": [
{"name": "Dump-state reports imported records", "type": "dump_state", "field": "importSummary.totalRecords", "expect": 1, "match": "min"},
{"name": "Imported rows persisted in SQLite", "type": "sqlite_count", "table": "messages", "min": 1}
